persons.name: Aaron Bacon
persons.harm: 16-year-old who died of acute peritonitis at North Star Expeditions in Utah in 1994 through negligence and lack of medical attention.

contacts.what_institution_did: Charged several staff, including the owners, with abuse and neglect; owners and a staffer pled guilty to negligent homicide and another staffer was convicted.

contacts.what_happened_next: Guilty pleas and a conviction followed.

contacts.quote: Another staffer, [perpetrator], was found guilty of felony abuse or neglect of a disabled child and sentenced to a year in jail and 36 months probation.
contacts.what_happened_next: Sentences imposed.

persons.outcome_quote: Although the death was medically considered natural causes, it was a result of negligence and lack of medical attention.
persons.notes: Background case in host narration. Died from the harm, so the convictions are recorded as contacts but outcome is not_protected.

persons.name: Lulu (Kids of North Jersey; transcribed 'Lulu Porter'/'Lulu Quarter'/'Lulu Corridor')
persons.harm: Signed into Kids of North Jersey at 13 in 1984 and held for 13 years, subjected to kidnappings, beatings, forced labour, forced false confessions and restraint on the floor for hours.
persons.perpetrator_role: the program's founder, his wife and an assistant director

contacts.when: 2003 lawsuit, after the programs were closed
contacts.what_was_asked: Damages from the founder, his wife and an assistant director.
contacts.what_institution_did: Heard her civil lawsuit; she was ultimately awarded a $6.5 million settlement.
contacts.quote: Ultimately, Lulu was awarded a $6.5 million settlement.
contacts.what_happened_next: Award made; no criminal action described.
contacts.notes: Separately, New Jersey sued the founder for Medicaid overbilling and the program was shut down (1999), but that action was not prompted by her and was about billing, so it is not recorded as her contact.

persons.outcome_quote: In August 1997, Lulu finally escaped the kids' program.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: the award came about six years after she escaped
persons.notes: Host narration plus Maia Szalavitz interview. Harm ended because she escaped (not institutional action), so the later civil award is recorded as a contact but the outcome is not_protected. Evidence types: narration of a civil outcome (settlement) only; no conviction.

persons.name: Danielle Bregoli
persons.harm: Referred at 13 by Dr. Phil to Turnabout Ranch, Utah; reports being taken in the night, handcuffed, sleep and food deprived and witnessing restraints and violence.

persons.outcome_quote: Despite Dr. Phil's deflection, Burgoli and fellow Turnabout Ranch survivor Hannah Archiletta continue to partner with the nonprofit Breaking Code Silence, using their experiences to advocate for reform
persons.notes: Background case. She spoke out publicly (YouTube) and demanded an apology from Dr. Phil, who responded in a TV interview; neither is an institution with a duty to respond under the instructions. No report to police, licensing or courts is described.

persons.name: Leanne (Trails Carolina)

Leanne says her memories were later 'validated through like documents or other people's recounts'. Her own confrontation on the call (mother admitted hitting) contributed. Evidence: documents referred to, not read on air -> coded document_read_on_air is generous; flagged.

Granted, she had turned 18, but she was still a student there and under his care. They found out, and they banned him from the campus. The girl was ostracized and removed as well.

contacts.notes: Also fits blamed_punished_or_counter_accused (student removed and ostracised).

persons.outcome_quote: They found out, and they banned him from the campus. The girl was ostracized and removed as well.
persons.decisive_work_quote: They found out, and they banned him from the campus.
persons.notes: Told by Kat (witness, not the person). Abuser removed (protection) but the institution simultaneously punished her, so partly_protected with harmed_by_institution_ever true.

persons.name: Molly (mother)
persons.harm: After her parents' divorce her mother, drinking heavily, called her a slut, liar and fat, and once pinned her down and slammed her face into a brick entryway, bruising her; she also had Molly put in a 72-hour hold.
persons.outcome_quote: He just said, nobody should do that to you. That's not okay. But nobody could save me.
persons.notes: During the face-slamming the mother told a son to 'call the police' (seemingly against Molly); whether police came is not said. The mother also placed Molly in a 72-hour hold facility; whether the mother's violence was raised there is not said. An adult-era therapist later apologised for her role, having not known the family's other side. Coded reach unclear with no contacts.

persons.name: Molly (Turning Winds program)
persons.harm: At 13, left by deception at Turning Winds, Idaho (2002, ~6 months): forced manual labour logging for the owners' firewood business, military-style exercise until hands bled, talking bans for weeks, punished for asking for soap, bathroom doors opened by men, mail censored, forced false admissions.

contacts.what_was_asked: To tell her mother the program was not what she thought and get help.
contacts.what_institution_did: Tore up the letter and punished her for trying.
contacts.quote: It would immediately be tossed aside, torn up, and then I was punished for even trying to attempt to tell my mom anything.
contacts.what_happened_next: No phone contact until Thanksgiving.

contacts.what_institution_did: Interviewed her about working and clothing conditions at the facility; no action on conditions is described.
contacts.quote: The police department did call me after I got home to interview me about the facility and ask me direct questions like what were the working conditions like, what was your clothing situation like?
contacts.what_happened_next: Her mother stopped further interviews without an attorney.

contacts.what_institution_did: Her mother was, she believes, repaid in a settlement.
contacts.quote: My mom took legal action to get the money back that she spent to put me there. And I do believe that she was given that money back in settlement.
contacts.what_happened_next: Program continues to operate and expand.

persons.outcome_quote: The facility is bigger, nicer.
persons.notes: She left because her mother called an attorney after the staff arrest (family action, not an institution), so not_protected. Host narration also covers the founders' revoked foster licence and a 2005 child-endangerment case that was dropped (others_mentioned).

persons.name: Molly (Turning Winds staff member)
persons.harm: At 13, a night-watch staff member promoted to day staff groomed her, sexually harassed residents, pressured them into sexual acts while he watched, and repeatedly raped and tortured her, threatening to kill and bury anyone who told.

quotes.quote: I will hunt you down like a dog and kill you and bury you in the woods and no one will find you.
it didn't even register to me that I was being sexually abused. It just felt like one more thing to be scared of.

contacts.institution: Turning Winds (a direct-care staff member of the owner family)
contacts.what_institution_did: Discovered the staff member had been turning off cameras, questioned residents, called police and had him arrested.
contacts.quote: my abuser has been turning off the cameras for every single one of his shifts. There is no footage. What has been going on? here.
contacts.what_happened_next: Police called.

contacts.what_institution_did: Arrested him and took individual statements sensitively.
contacts.quote: They called the police and had him arrested. We didn't tell the police everything. They took statements individually. There was a lot of timeline questioning and they were very sensitive. I was very grateful to them.
contacts.what_happened_next: Charges followed.

contacts.what_institution_did: Sent parents a vague letter omitting sexual acts and stripped Molly of her graduation status so she would have to start over.
contacts.quote: they were stripping me of my graduation status, and I was going to have to start all over, which also means that they would get six more months of money out of my mother.
contacts.what_happened_next: Her mother called an attorney and she went home two days later.
contacts.notes: Also protected_itself (vague letter: 'I do remember them not mentioning any sexual acts whatsoever'). Document = letter she saw on screen, paraphrased.

contacts.what_institution_did: Charged him with direct harm to a child; trial held with other residents testifying; sentenced to days in jail and released early.
contacts.quote: He was actually sentenced to days in jail and then somehow got out earlier.
contacts.what_happened_next: He was later arrested and imprisoned on unrelated charges.

persons.outcome_quote: They called the police and had him arrested.
persons.decisive_work_quote: One of the brothers, he was direct care staff. He barged in the door and there was another resident.
persons.notes: The abuse was stopped by the institution's own discovery and the arrest. The residents (including Molly) told only part of what happened. She was subpoenaed but her mother kept her from testifying. Two girls on suicide watch were also abused (others_mentioned).

persons.name: Danielle (Second Nature Blue Ridge)
persons.harm: At 15, sent for 8 weeks (Dec 2004-Feb 2005) to a Georgia wilderness program under the pretext of a three-week camp: forced from the car, strip searched, slept between strangers, punished by restarting phases, left with an untreated open wound; she injured her own arm trying to get out.

quotes.quote: Absolutely not. They would believe these therapists and counselors over. anything I had to say.
When I realized, wow, some of the stuff was really messed up in my late 30s is like just now dawning on me how not okay and not normal these experiences were.

persons.outcome_quote: I know my parents will never acknowledge what I went through during these times.
persons.notes: Pseudonym. Program (now Blue Ridge Therapeutic Wilderness) gave a statement denying that the listed practices are accurate; this is institution_statement, not corroboration. She told a counselor her parents didn't know what this was; the counselor said they did (about placement, not abuse).

persons.name: Danielle (Carlbrook School)
persons.harm: 18 months at Carlbrook School, Virginia: strip search, public shaming, 'railing' attack groups, mandated cuddle piles with staff, six weeks of isolation and punitive running/labour, workshops off medication, her baby picture placed among 'scary' props.

quotes.quote: I stopped saying I didn't want to be there because that would only prolong my stay or make it more painful.
He basically was an ear to all of our phone calls monitoring the content of our phone calls.

persons.outcome_quote: And up until this point, I have not had somebody either willing to listen, wanting to understand, to empathize, to believe me.
persons.notes: 'fear_of_abuser' used for fear of the institution (longer stay). She read from her red punishment notebook. Carlbrook closed 2015 citing enrollment.

persons.name: Danielle (parents)
persons.harm: Grew up unwanted and body-shamed: her mother dismissed a broken elbow and her request for help with bulimia, her father told her to retract a suicide disclosure, and her mother hesitated to come home when she overdosed.

quotes.quote: Up until my mid-30s, I looked as my parents as being the perfect parents.

persons.outcome_quote: I've had to, like, as an adult, I just accept my parents for who they are
persons.notes: She saw a therapist (bulimia) and was hospitalised for an overdose, but the parental treatment itself is not described as raised with those providers.

persons.name: Kalin
persons.harm: At Academy at Ivy Ridge (Mar 2006-Aug 2007, from 14): isolation room and forced repetitive writing, levels dropped, calls cut off and punished when she complained about food and heat; possibly harmed by a female staff member she would not talk about.

contacts.institution: Academy at Ivy Ridge (her family rep)
contacts.what_was_asked: n/a (she mentioned bad food/no heat to her parents on a monitored call).
contacts.what_institution_did: Ended the call, told the parents she was lying to manipulate them and that she would be punished.
contacts.quote: And Kaelin's going to get a consequence for lying. We didn't even consider that she was telling the truth.
contacts.what_happened_next: Parents believed the program; she stayed until her mother pulled her in Aug 2007.

persons.outcome_quote: I found out while I was cheering her on and I'm doing my program, she was suffering.
persons.notes: Told by her mother Shannon. Kalin died in 2017 (her mother suspects foul play; not linked to the program). Her mother removed her (family action). Her files, including journals and a therapist note, were later retrieved and read from on air. The St. Lawrence County DA's general Ivy Ridge investigation (no charges) is not prompted by her and is noted in others_mentioned.

persons.name: Ed
persons.harm: At 17, dragged from bed by transporters and hog-tied in handcuffs, then at Academy at Ivy Ridge (Oct 2002-Jul 2003) thrown around by the director while forced to shave, witnessed constant violent restraints, and denied dental care for seven months until a tooth rotted; given a fake diploma.
persons.perpetrator_role: Ivy Ridge director and staff; transport company

quotes.quote: So if you said anything negative towards anybody or the program, they would immediately hang up the phone. and then you would get tossed down to observe placement and restrained and manhandled.

contacts.institution: State of New York / New York Board of Education (attempted lawsuit)
contacts.when: 2025, about three weeks before the interview
contacts.what_institution_did: Received a letter that the claim could not proceed because of the statute of limitations.
contacts.quote: but about three weeks ago we got a letter saying they can't proceed with it. They just cite statute of limitations.
contacts.what_happened_next: No legal route; he continues advocacy (helped close a Nevada program).
contacts.notes: Who sent the letter (court, state or their attorneys) is not specified.

persons.outcome_quote: Apparently, we're too late, so somebody else has to do it.
persons.notes: He screamed that he was kidnapped at a rest stop; bystanders did nothing (not an institution). He told his father on release that kids were being severely abused; his father did not believe him. His parents tried and failed to sue over the fake diploma. Documents: Ivy Ridge files and incident reports shared after the documentary (shown on his social media post, about another student).

persons.name: Julie
persons.harm: At 13, Academy at Ivy Ridge (2005-2006): strip searched while menstruating, screamed at, threatened with isolation, forced to write a false confession of drug use and sex that was sent to her parents, denied level advancement to keep her past a year, gained 50 pounds and stopped menstruating.

contacts.institution: Academy at Ivy Ridge (family reps/letter screening)
contacts.what_was_asked: To tell her parents she was miserable / what was happening (kids beaten, not fed).
contacts.what_institution_did: Passed some letters but used them to tell parents she was manipulating them and was not ready to come home.
contacts.quote: They would use that letter to show my parents, even though she's making progress, we warned you that your child's going to manipulate you.
contacts.what_happened_next: She stayed until her parents pulled her at one year.

persons.outcome_quote: All the staff members that were involved, there was never a consequence for them.
persons.notes: Her retrieved file includes program emails (one read on air, with racist remarks about her family). Never reported later: 'nobody really thought about it as this is a really bad thing that happened. Maybe you should report it.' Statutes of limitations cited.

persons.name: Marie (Academy at Ivy Ridge)
persons.harm: At 17, taken by transporters under a dentist pretext to Academy at Ivy Ridge (Apr 2005-Dec 2006): forced to eat raw bacon, denied medical/dental care for 20 months, attack therapy, arbitrary 'drops', denied church, pressured to sign away rights past 18, letters redacted.

contacts.what_institution_did: Redacted the complaints from her letter.
contacts.quote: I think they redacted a lot of my letter because you're not allowed to complain about the facility at all.
contacts.what_happened_next: Stayed 20 months.

contacts.institution: Academy at Ivy Ridge grievance process
contacts.what_institution_did: Never overturned any of her grievances.
contacts.quote: There's a grievance process, but I was never overturned on any of my cases, which were all very valid.
contacts.what_happened_next: Drops continued.

contacts.institution: campus counselor at the Honor Academy (Texas)
contacts.what_institution_did: Identified acute post-traumatic stress and taught a coping skill.
contacts.quote: I first learned there that that's called acute post-traumatic stress disorder.
contacts.what_happened_next: Later informal college counseling.

persons.outcome_quote: I think not being believed was the hardest part.
persons.notes: She left after 20 months on finishing the program. The counselor contact is support after harm ended, not protection.

persons.name: Marie (father)
persons.harm: Her father dragged her upstairs by the foot at 9, shoved and punched her, threw her onto concrete, pushed her down stairs and choked her; with her stepmother he 'interrogated' and punished her, and sent her to Ivy Ridge when she planned to move to her aunt's.

quotes.quote: And I was trying to deny it. I actually always defended my parents.

contacts.what_institution_did: Heard her account of the situation at home and kept driving.
contacts.quote: They looked at each other and, and one of them said, should we turn around? And then they were just like, no, let's keep going.
contacts.what_happened_next: Delivered to Ivy Ridge.

contacts.institution: Academy at Ivy Ridge (dorm parent in group)
contacts.what_was_asked: To be believed that she did not deserve to be there and her parents were unreasonable.
contacts.what_institution_did: Told her there were two sides and she was playing the victim; peers said they didn't believe her.
contacts.quote: You can't go by your story alone. You're probably just playing the victim right now,
contacts.what_happened_next: She felt disbelieved throughout.

contacts.institution: a family therapist (virtual joint session with her father)
contacts.what_institution_did: Told her the father was not ready, willing or able to engage.
contacts.quote: The therapist was like, your dad is not ready, willing or able to do this. This man is very detached from you.
contacts.what_happened_next: Minimal contact with father; he has not apologised.

persons.outcome_quote: My dad still hasn't apologized.
persons.notes: Journal kept from freshman year (mentioned; partly recounted). Neighbour children witnessed abuse; aunts and uncles staged an intervention (family). A teacher may have shown her parents her 'how to run away' essay instead of asking if things were okay at home (unclear; not coded). Harm stopped because she was sent away, not by institutional action.

persons.name: Anthony
persons.harm: Sexually assaulted while at Academy at Ivy Ridge (Aug 2003-Mar 2004, age 17), after being taken by teen escorts; he disclosed it only 18 years later and died by suicide the next day.
persons.perpetrator_role: not specified (at Academy at Ivy Ridge)

quotes.quote: He was embarrassed.

contacts.what_institution_did: Received his disclosure; what the therapist did is not described.
contacts.quote: And he said the only two people that knew were his current therapist that he was going to. And he told me, and that's it in his life.
contacts.what_happened_next: He died by suicide on October 26.

persons.outcome_quote: And he said, we did this to him. And I said, I know we did this to him. That was October 26th.
persons.notes: Told by his mother Terry. Delay reason 'other' = embarrassment, and per his mother 'he didn't want it out there'. His mother believes the program caused his death.

persons.name: Katie (rape at 14)
persons.harm: At 14, after drinking for the first time, raped while unconscious by a boy she had met online; she learned of it from a hospital nurse.

quotes.quote: I was embarrassed and I was afraid of any social backlash.

contacts.what_was_asked: Medical care (friend's mother brought her in).
contacts.what_institution_did: Treated her; a nurse asked about protection, which is how she learned she had been raped. No report or further step is described.
contacts.quote: a nurse had asked me about whether or not I wore protection. I didn't know what she was talking about. And that's how I found out that I had been raped.
contacts.what_happened_next: Her mother called the boy's parents, who denied it; nothing else changed.

persons.outcome_quote: That mother was like, not my sons, never my sons. I just dove deeper into depression.
persons.notes: harmed_by_institution_ever true because at Island View her therapist made her describe the rape to about 40 boys (an exposure of this harm by an institution). No police contact mentioned.

persons.name: Katie (stepfather)
persons.harm: From about age 6 to 8 her stepfather, who had explosive anger, was physically violent to her and her sister.

quotes.quote: I didn't know that this was not normal.

persons.outcome_quote: he had hurt my sister bad enough that my dad became aware of the abuse and he uprooted us and moved us back to the city he lived in.
persons.notes: Her father removed them; no institution mentioned.

persons.name: Katie (Island View RTC)
persons.harm: At 14, eight months at Island View RTC, Utah (2004): locked building, confrontation groups, social isolation 'yellow zone' even when sick, mattress in a lit hallway, monitored calls, and her therapist made her describe her rape to about 40 boys.

quotes.quote: But if kids' phone calls are monitored and they have no way of reaching authorities, there's no way to file or purport an allegation that would then require investigation.

persons.outcome_quote: When I read about these lawsuits, the people who sued Island View, the people who are suing elevations, and I read other survivors' stories, and they match my own.
persons.notes: She told her father on the first monitored call that the treatment wasn't right; he had been prepped to disbelieve her (family). Journals read from on air.

persons.name: Katie (Oakley School)
persons.harm: Sent straight from Island View to the Oakley School (Utah, ~12 months): social isolation punishments, silent punitive hikes, days-long 'come clean' interrogations, letters from friends withheld and thrown away, made to tell her story to every class at her home school.

quotes.quote: My friends had been writing me letters and they withheld the letters. Then threw them away when I graduated.

persons.outcome_quote: There wasn't a lot of protection.
persons.notes: Same parent company as Island View. Closed 2017.

persons.name: Nicole
persons.harm: At 15, sent to the DeSisto School, Massachusetts (1994-1996): no stall doors and group naked showers, nightly attack-therapy dorm meetings run by unqualified staff, 'farm' punishment and unpaid labour (including in the founder's paid dinner theatre), lithium toxicity from misdiagnosis, and the founder exposing himself in a robe.

quotes.quote: There was somebody always listening on your end. So it wasn't that I could tell them things that were going on.

persons.outcome_quote: I ran away at 18 because I knew they couldn't keep me.
persons.notes: Massachusetts child-care regulators investigated from 2000 and the school closed in June 2004 after state findings, years after she left; not prompted by her, so not coded as her contact. A later hospital psychologist corrected her bipolar misdiagnosis to PTSD (medical, about diagnosis, not a report of the harm).

persons.name: Brittany
persons.harm: Taken at night by transporters threatening handcuffs to Tranquility Bay, Jamaica (from May 2005): lockdown concrete facility, punishments for looking at the ocean, restraints with knees on backs, an untreated ear infection for two weeks, conditional family support tied to finishing the program.

quotes.quote: You want to join? And I was like, no, because I never had that experience.

persons.outcome_quote: My parents see it as Jamaica saved my life.
persons.notes: She tried to signal for help at the airport during transport; the escorts cut off a stranger's approach. She declined to join lawsuits. Journal and letters read on air. Left at 18 after a drop; program closed 2009.

persons.name: Haley (Utah wilderness program)
persons.harm: At 15, taken from her home by transporters (handcuffed, legs held) to a Utah wilderness program in January: strip searched, left alone in snow with no instruction, unable to make fire (bone disease) so no hot food, no bathing for six weeks; her therapist joked about her suicidal impulse.

quotes.quote: I don't remember anything positive about that experience.

persons.outcome_quote: I'm thinking, I love that my trauma is a joke to you.
persons.notes: She told the therapist she wanted to jump off the cliff after he said her parents did not want her home; that is a disclosure of distress, not a report of the abuse.

persons.name: Haley (Montana boarding school)
persons.harm: About two years at an unnamed Montana therapeutic boarding school (~2000-2002): heavy unpaid labour (horses, fences, clear-cutting, firewood sold to neighbours), pain dismissed, forced sexual and other 'histories' shared with parents without consent, a cardboard 'victim triangle' worn for a year, 'interventions' living outdoors.

contacts.what_was_asked: Relief from pain caused by the labour.
contacts.what_institution_did: Told her the pain was repressed emotion to be dealt with in (attack) therapy.
contacts.quote: It was, it's not physical pain. It is repressed emotions that you're not dealing with.
contacts.what_happened_next: Labour continued.

persons.outcome_quote: So much of what we did there physically hurt us.
persons.notes: She got out by persisting about bone pain until an X-ray led a doctor to recommend a specialist and her mother insisted; that medical contact was about her bone condition, not the abuse. School's attorneys deny all allegations (institution_statement). Dylan corroborates the school's practices (second_witness). Journals and her mother's letters read from.

persons.name: Haley (parents)
persons.harm: Grew up amid her parents' frequent violence toward each other; her mother backed her into corners and her parents held her down (mother holding, father sitting on her back) during fights.

contacts.what_institution_did: Responded to fights; her mother told them Haley was the violent one. What police then did is not stated.
contacts.quote: the police being called, usually by the neighbors, and them showing up and me thinking, now my mom's going to tell them that was my father, and she's told them that it was me.
contacts.what_happened_next: Violence continued until her father moved out.

contacts.what_institution_did: Told her mother the home was unhealthy and Haley was acting out because of it; no protective step described.
contacts.quote: the therapist is telling my mother how unhealthy our home is and that I'm acting out because of that.
contacts.what_happened_next: No change described.

persons.outcome_quote: I feel the need to protect my dad and my mom and say that I was ever like beaten, but there was physical violence in her home.
persons.notes: Document = her mother's journals describing the therapy (read/paraphrased on air). The police response may have amounted to counter-accusing Haley, but the transcript does not say what police did.

persons.name: Dylan (attempted rape at Hyde School)
persons.harm: In ninth grade at Hyde School, Maine, another student sexually assaulted him and attempted to rape him.

quotes.quote: I told my parents, they didn't believe me. That was really hard. They really thought that it was just another ploy for me to go home.

persons.outcome_quote: I just wanted this kid held accountable, and expelled for trying to rape me. I was done. I ran away again.
persons.notes: Whether the school learned of it is not said; Dylan himself was then expelled for running away. His parents apologised years later.

persons.name: Dylan (Montana boarding school)
persons.harm: After a 5-week Oregon wilderness program (Catherine Freer: 23-24 mile hikes, starvation diet), about two years at the same unnamed Montana school as Haley (mid-1990s): denied bathroom use causing bladder damage, three months of solitary 'intervention' building a corral alone, tied to another student for a week, no medical care for sun poisoning, open communal outhouse.
persons.perpetrator_role: the school's head and staff (and wilderness staff)

contacts.institution: Montana school (his assigned therapist on monitored call)
contacts.what_was_asked: To tell his parents there was abuse going on.
contacts.what_institution_did: Hung up the phone immediately.
contacts.quote: I do remember one time being on the phone with my parents trying to tell them there was abuse going on and hung up the phone immediately.
contacts.what_happened_next: Stayed until expelled after running away.

contacts.what_institution_did: Found he was 'not crazy' and arranged a less abusive placement (John Dewey Academy).
contacts.quote: I had expressed to him how all I wanted was to go to not such an abusive program. I said, ultimately, I want to go back home, but I guess that's really not an option, so I just want to go to someplace more like hide. He accomplished that for me.
contacts.what_happened_next: At John Dewey he was isolated after running; he ran away to New York.

persons.outcome_quote: It took me until I was 32 years old to get my life together. And that right there is the real impact of these programs.
persons.notes: Wilderness and John Dewey harms folded into this record (lighter). Haley corroborates the Montana school (second_witness). Expulsion, not institutional protection, ended the Montana placement. School's attorneys deny allegations.

persons.name: Dylan (Western Samoa program)
persons.harm: At 17, sent to a lockdown program in Western Samoa where he describes a lot of physical and sexual abuse; at 18 the owner initially refused his passport, claiming he was a Samoan citizen until 24.
persons.perpetrator_role: the Samoa program's owners and staff

contacts.when: on his 18th birthday, after leaving the program
contacts.what_institution_did: Listened to his whole story and flew him to the U.S. West Coast.
contacts.quote: He sat with me for a long time and just listened. And at the end of it, he was like, let's get you back on the mainland at least. He said, I can fly you as far as the West Coast.
contacts.what_happened_next: Flew to Arizona; lived with a friend, later got his GED and degree.

persons.outcome_quote: If you do not give me my passport today, I will sue you. And he did. And then he asked me to please not tell anybody that they would address it.
persons.notes: He ended the harm himself by demanding his passport at 18 (a sympathetic counselor sheltered him). The embassy helped afterwards; since the harm was ended by his own action, outcome not_protected (could be argued partly_protected).

persons.name: Max (SageWalk Wilderness)
persons.harm: At 14 (2007), taken from bed at 2:30am by transporters to SageWalk in Oregon for 58 days: blindfolded, threatened not to tell anyone, toe permanently disfigured with no medical care, food scarcity, public 10-day suicide watch, forced to keep hiking while overheating.

contacts.what_was_asked: What happened that Max described in a letter.
contacts.what_institution_did: Told her father it was just a ploy to get home and not to believe anything negative.
contacts.quote: She described something that happened that wasn't good. And so I called Sage Walk about it. They're like, that's just them trying to get home. Don't believe anything they say that's negative.
contacts.what_happened_next: Max stayed 58 days and was funnelled to Mount Bachelor.

persons.outcome_quote: I lived in the fucking middle of the woods for 58 days of my life.
persons.notes: Father (who placed Max) is the second witness. SageWalk closed 2011 after another student's death (others_mentioned). Institution type 'other' = the abusing program itself.

persons.name: Max (Mount Bachelor Academy)
persons.harm: 2007-2009 at Mount Bachelor Academy, Oregon: secret 'Life Step' attack-therapy workshops, forced age regression, public humiliation drills, punitive labour 'self-studies', forced disclosure lists read to parents, medication withheld for some students, a winter trip on which staff got the group lost until the Forest Service rescued them.

contacts.what_was_asked: Response to things Max told him.
contacts.what_institution_did: Said it didn't happen and not to listen to Max.
contacts.quote: If she would tell me anything that didn't sound good and I would go talk to the Mount Bachelor people, they would say, oh, that didn't happen. and don't listen to them when they tell you that.
contacts.what_happened_next: Max stayed and graduated.

contacts.institution: court (custody hearing brought by Max's uncle)
contacts.when: after graduation, when Max was a minor living with aunt and uncle
contacts.what_was_asked: Uncle sought to send Max to another program.
contacts.what_institution_did: Refused because the uncle had no custody; Max was linked with a social worker, lawyer and advocate.
contacts.quote: So the judge basically laughed him out of the courtroom because I was a minor. I got LinkedIn with a social worker, a lawyer, an advocate,
contacts.what_happened_next: Plan made for Max to return to Mount Bachelor temporarily.
contacts.notes: Protective of Max against a further placement rather than a response to the program abuse.

contacts.what_institution_did: Investigated over seven months, interviewing students apart from staff; found abuse and neglect; licence suspended and school closed December 2009.
contacts.quote: There was a school nurse. She was the whistleblower who got that place shut down. She reported it to DHS.
contacts.what_happened_next: Max moved to a transitional youth program whose social worker helped her finish school.
contacts.notes: Staff coached compliant students like Max on what to tell DHS. 2010 settlement: MBA acknowledged DHS had reasonable basis (host narration).

persons.outcome_quote: Mount Bachelor was shut down in December of 2009. What ended up happening was that this program offered to take me in as an unhoused youth, essentially.
persons.decisive_work_quote: In 2009, the Oregon Department of Human Services, concluded a seven-month investigation, finding multiple instances of abuse and neglect, including sexualized role-playing, forced isolation, punitive labor, and other degrading acts. As a result, MBA's license was suspended
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: the state closed the school about two years after Max arrived
persons.notes: Max was back at MBA when DHS investigated and closed it, so the closure ended Max's exposure (protected). The report came from a staff nurse (third_party). Max's father did not let Max join the later lawsuit. Max read from program assignment notebooks; father found cost records. coder_notes:
Season 24 covers the so-called troubled teen industry (TTI): survivor interviews (Meg, Malia, Leanne, Lindy, Kat, Molly, Danielle, Ed, Julie, Marie, Katie, Nicole, Brittany, Haley, Dylan, Max), two parents whose children died (Shannon re Kalin; Terry re Anthony), expert episodes (Maia Szalavitz, Dr. Keating, Dr. Hartselle: no person stories), a case-and-community update (Season 18 update coded as a group record), and a What Came Next crossover (John Callas) published in the season feed. All 14 chunk files were read to their stated last line, across several sessions interrupted by usage limits; notes were written after each file.

Key coding decisions:
1. In most TTI stories the institution that harmed the child was the program itself. When a survivor raised the harm with program staff/therapists (or a parent did on their behalf), I recorded it as a contact with that institution (often noting institution_was_abusers), because the instructions count any organisation with power to respond. Where nothing was raised, I coded never_reached, mostly with institution_was_abusers (monitored calls and letters), did_not_know_it_was_abuse, or fear of a longer stay.
2. harmed_by_institution_ever is set true only where an institution responding to a disclosure (or otherwise acting on the person's harm) blamed, punished or exposed them, not merely because the program was the abuser; otherwise nearly every survivor would be true.
3. One record per harm by a different perpetrator: separate records for different programs where substantive harm is described, and for parental abuse or sexual assaults outside the programs. Some lighter placements were folded into a neighbouring record (Leanne: New Leaf + Pacific Quest; Dylan: Catherine Freer and John Dewey folded into the Montana record). Brief harms with no aftermath (e.g., John Callas's childhood rape by his sister's friend, Malia's adult assault, Danielle's mention of sexual assault, Kat's later assault, Nicole's abusive boyfriend) were not given records.
4. Background cases from host narration (Kristen Chase, Aaron Bacon, Lulu, Asheville Academy deaths, Red Rock Canyon student, Trails Carolina boy, Taylor Goodridge, Baruch Silvers, Paris Hilton, Danielle Bregoli, Hannah Archuleta, Island View 15-year-old) were given records because the season tells some of what was done and what followed; they are low/medium confidence. A different coder might put some in others_mentioned.
5. Regulator actions against programs that were not prompted by the person and came after they left (DeSisto closure 2004, Ivy Ridge DA investigation and AG settlement, Copper Canyon/Aspen issues) were not coded as that person's contacts; mentioned in notes. Exception: Max was still at Mount Bachelor when DHS investigated and closed it, so that is coded as Max's contact and protection.
6. Parents' calls/letters to the program on the child's behalf are coded as contacts initiated by family_or_friends (e.g., Max's father to SageWalk and Mount Bachelor).
7. Where harm ended because the person aged out, ran away, was pulled by a parent, or left by their own action, later institutional actions are not protection (not_protected), per instructions.
8. Names: perpetrators' and accused persons' names in quotes were replaced with [perpetrator]. Quotes naming non-victims (family members, attorneys, a senator, therapists) were avoided by choosing other passages. Parents who placed children (Shannon, Terry, Max's father) were not given person records as harmed persons, although the season frames them as deceived and financially exploited.
9. Sources were computed by locating each quote in the transcript text; the timestamp is the bracketed marker of the line where the quote begins. Spelling of names follows the transcript where it varies (e.g., Lulu's surname).
10. No unassigned episode concerned this season; only INDEX.txt was read.
